_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Zambia covering Bantu migration, Lozi/Bemba kingdoms, Livingstone/Victoria Falls, Northern Rhodesia, copper belt, Kaunda/UNIP, Chiluba multiparty transition, and copper dependency.

religion.note: Constitution declares Zambia a 'Christian nation' (1991 amendment)

ethnic_groups.name: Bemba
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern/Copperbelt provinces; Bantu; Bemba Kingdom (Chitimukulu paramount chief); largest group; mining/urban dominant; Bemba language widely spoken beyond ethnic Bemba

ethnic_groups.name: Tonga
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Province; Bantu; cattle pastoralists; displaced by Kariba Dam 1958; Tonga Plateau; agricultural

ethnic_groups.name: Chewa (Nyanja)
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Province; Bantu; cross-border with Malawi/Mozambique; Gule Wamkulu secret society (UNESCO); Nyanja lingua franca in Lusaka

ethnic_groups.name: Lozi (Barotse)
ethnic_groups.notes: Western Province; Barotseland Kingdom; Litunga (king); Kuomboka ceremony (UNESCO); Barotseland Agreement 1964; separatist sentiment

ethnic_groups.name: Nsenga
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Province; Bantu; farming; Petauke area

ethnic_groups.name: Tumbuka
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern/Northern; Bantu; cross-border with Malawi; historically Ngoni-influenced

ethnic_groups.name: Ngoni
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Province; Bantu; Zulu origin (Mfecane migration); warrior heritage; Mpezeni paramount chief; adopted Chewa language

ethnic_groups.name: Lala
ethnic_groups.notes: Central Province; Bantu; Serenje/Mkushi; Lala-Bisa grouping; farming

ethnic_groups.name: Kaonde
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwestern Province; Bantu; one of the seven 'official' language groups; mining area

ethnic_groups.name: Lunda
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwestern Province; Bantu; cross-border with DR Congo/Angola; Lunda Empire heritage; Mwata Kazembe

ethnic_groups.name: Luvale
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwestern Province; Bantu; Makishi masquerade (UNESCO); cross-border with Angola

ethnic_groups.name: Mambwe-Lungu
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Province; Lake Tanganyika area; farming/fishing

ethnic_groups.name: Namwanga
ethnic_groups.notes: Muchinga/Northern; Bantu; cross-border with Tanzania; Nakonde area

ethnic_groups.name: Other (70+ groups)
ethnic_groups.notes: Ila, Lenje, Soli, Bisa, Tabwa, Ushi, Mbunda, Nkoya, Tokaleya, and others; 73 ethnic groups / 7 official language groups; Zambia is notably peaceful inter-ethnically

current_leader.name: Hakainde Hichilema
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: UPND; Tonga; businessman (cattle ranching); defeated Lungu in landslide after 6th attempt; economic reform focus; debt restructuring

former_presidents.name: Kenneth Kaunda
former_presidents.notes: Father of the Nation; UNIP; one-party state from 1972; 'KK'; Zambian humanism; copper nationalisation; frontline state against apartheid; peacefully accepted multiparty election loss 1991; died 2021

former_presidents.name: Frederick Chiluba
former_presidents.notes: MMD; trade unionist; declared Zambia a 'Christian nation'; privatisation; tried to change constitution for third term; corruption convictions posthumously

former_presidents.name: Levy Mwanawasa
former_presidents.notes: MMD; anti-corruption drive; prosecuted Chiluba; died in office (stroke) August 2008

former_presidents.name: Rupiah Banda
former_presidents.notes: MMD; VP who succeeded Mwanawasa; lost to Sata 2011

former_presidents.name: Michael Sata
former_presidents.notes: PF; 'King Cobra'; populist; died in office October 2014

former_presidents.name: Edgar Lungu
former_presidents.notes: PF; completed Sata's term then won 2016; authoritarian drift; debt distress; lost to Hichilema 2021

910.name: Early Peoples and Bantu Migration
910.description: Khoisan hunter-gatherers; Bantu migration introduces farming, iron-working, and new linguistic families to the Zambian plateau.

sub_clusters.name: Khoisan Hunter-Gatherer Communities
sub_clusters.description: San/Khoisan peoples as earliest inhabitants; Later Stone Age sites; Nachikufu cave culture.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Migration into Zambia
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking peoples migrate into Zambia bringing iron smelting, pottery, and settled agriculture; displacement of Khoisan.

sub_clusters.name: Iron Age Societies
sub_clusters.description: Chondwe, Kalambo Falls, and Ingombe Ilede archaeological sites; early copper smelting; long-distance trade emerges.

920.name: Pre-Colonial Kingdoms and Chiefdoms
920.description: Development of major kingdoms: Lozi (Barotseland), Bemba, Lunda, Kazembe; trade networks linking central and southern Africa.

sub_clusters.name: Lozi Kingdom (Barotseland)
sub_clusters.description: Lozi Kingdom of the Zambezi floodplain; Litunga (king); annual Kuomboka ceremony; sophisticated flood management.

sub_clusters.name: Bemba Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: Bemba Kingdom of the Crocodile Clan; paramount chief Chitimukulu; territorial expansion; ivory and slave trade.

sub_clusters.name: Lunda-Kazembe Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: Eastern Lunda Kingdom of Kazembe in Luapula valley; trade links to both Atlantic and Indian Ocean coasts.

sub_clusters.name: Ingombe Ilede and Long-Distance Trade
sub_clusters.description: Ingombe Ilede archaeological site on Zambezi; evidence of cross-continental gold, copper, and cloth trade.

930.name: European Exploration and Missionary Era
930.description: David Livingstone's explorations; Victoria Falls discovery; missionary stations; Lozi-British relations; slave trade disruption.

sub_clusters.name: Livingstone and Victoria Falls
sub_clusters.description: David Livingstone reaches Mosi-oa-Tunya (Victoria Falls) 1855; transcontinental journey; anti-slave trade advocacy.

sub_clusters.name: Missionary Stations
sub_clusters.description: Paris Evangelical Mission in Barotseland; London Missionary Society; White Fathers; Christianity and literacy introduced.

sub_clusters.name: Slave Trade and Its Disruption
sub_clusters.description: Arab-Swahili and Portuguese slave trading in eastern Zambia; Livingstone's campaigns; British anti-slavery intervention.

940.name: Northern Rhodesia (Colonial Period)
940.description: BSAC charter; Northern Rhodesia colony; copper belt development; Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland; African resistance.

sub_clusters.name: BSAC and Colonial Conquest
sub_clusters.description: British South Africa Company secures mineral rights through treaties; amalgamation of North-Western and North-Eastern Rhodesia 1911; Crown colony 1924.

sub_clusters.name: Copper Belt Development
sub_clusters.description: Major copper deposits exploited from 1928; migrant labour system; copper belt towns; African mine workers' unions.

sub_clusters.name: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland
sub_clusters.description: Central African Federation imposed despite African opposition; copper revenues benefit Southern Rhodesia; dissolution 1963.

sub_clusters.name: UNIP and Independence Movement
sub_clusters.description: Kenneth Kaunda leads UNIP; Cha Cha Cha civil disobedience campaign; independence 24 October 1964.

950.name: Kaunda and One-Party State
950.description: Kaunda's humanist one-party state; nationalisation; front-line state against apartheid; copper price collapse; economic crisis.

sub_clusters.name: Kaunda's Zambian Humanism
sub_clusters.description: Kenneth Kaunda first president; Zambian Humanism philosophy; nationalisation of mines (Zambia Industrial and Mining Corporation).

sub_clusters.name: One-Party State
sub_clusters.description: Second Republic; UNIP sole legal party; authoritarian governance; economic mismanagement; opposition suppressed.

sub_clusters.name: Front-Line State Against Apartheid
sub_clusters.description: Zambia hosts ANC, SWAPO, and Zimbabwean liberation movements; Rhodesian and South African attacks; TAZARA railway built with Chinese aid.

sub_clusters.name: Copper Price Collapse
sub_clusters.description: Global copper price crash devastates economy; GDP decline; mounting debt; IMF structural adjustment; food riots 1986-1990.

960.name: Multiparty Zambia and Modern Era
960.description: Chiluba democratic transition; copper privatisation; presidential term debates; Lungu; Hichilema; economic diversification efforts.

sub_clusters.name: Chiluba and Democratic Transition
sub_clusters.description: Frederick Chiluba's MMD defeats Kaunda in multiparty elections 1991; economic liberalisation; copper mine privatisation; corruption.

sub_clusters.name: Copper Dependency and Diversification
sub_clusters.description: Copper supercycle benefits then challenges Zambia; Chinese investment; debt crisis; diversification into agriculture and tourism.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Consolidation Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Mwanawasa, Banda, Sata, Lungu presidencies; third-term debates; Hichilema wins 2021; democratic renewal.

sub_clusters.name: Debt Crisis and IMF Programme
sub_clusters.description: Zambia defaults on Eurobond debt November 2020; first African COVID-era sovereign default; IMF programme; debt restructuring.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
